summary: Grammar is clean (no flags, nothing missed) and this version has the plainest vocabulary of the three: no unknown word without a gloss or a known-word paraphrase. Quality issues only: 'lagen' for rows of books, the envelope form 'meneer H. Potter', an unnecessary gloss on kaft and one afterthought comma in b013.

findings.fragment: twee lagen sciencefiction … De achterste laag boeken … de achterste laag
findings.problem: Books standing front and back on a shelf stand 'in twee rijen' in Dutch; 'lagen' suggests horizontal strata, and for a learner the form collides with the imperfectum of liggen while laag is known mainly as 'low'.
findings.evidence: lexicon: laag A2 glossed 'low'; rij A2; V1 and V3 use rijen; EN 'back layer … above the books in front' describes rows
findings.required_fix: 'Andere planken hebben twee rijen sciencefiction met een zachte kaft. De achterste rij staat op oude tissuedozen\authorsnotefootnotemark{} of op stukken hout. Zo kun je de achterste rij boven de voorste boeken zien.'

findings.problem: kaft is a known A2 word; the gloss is noise.
findings.required_fix: Write 'boeken met een harde kaft' without \gl.

findings.problem: On an envelope Dutch writes 'De heer' / 'Dhr.', never 'meneer'; the formal green-ink address reads childish here.
